name: Zig
about: What Zig is, and its colours, from a grammar built on your machine
_about: The worked example of a plugin that brings its own syntax highlighting.
textfold knows nothing about Zig; this is the whole of teaching it,
and none of it is a change to the editor.
textfold --install zig
Two files do it. `highlights.scm` is published here and lands beside
this manifest when the plugin is installed. `zig.so` is not published:
it is a compiled shared library, it would have to be one per platform,
and building it is four lines of install steps — fetch the grammar's C,
compile it, throw the C away.
`${plugin}` is the directory this has been installed to, which is how
the manifest names its own two files without knowing where that is.
`needs` is a path rather than a program name. A bare name is looked up
on the PATH and has to be runnable; a path only has to be there, which
is what a shared library is — so the plugins list says `needs` until
the library has actually been built, rather than saying `on` beside a
language with no colours.
There is no language server here. Adding zls is three more lines:
"needs": ["zls"],
"languages": { "zig": { "servers": [
{ "name": "zls", "command": "zls", "roots": ["build.zig"] } ] } }
but that is what the other fourteen plugins here are examples of, and
this one is about the grammar.
